title: Sequence-Scallop: adaptive scallop batching to reduce padding and guide kernel selection
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Prefill-heavy workloads with broad sequence-length variance waste GPU cycles due to padding and cause suboptimal kernel choices. Goal: implement an adaptive 'scallop' bucketing and micro-batch shaping system that (1) reduces per-request padding by splitting/merging sequences into shallow scallops, (2) emits kernel-hint metadata so scheduler picks the optimal attention kernel and tensor layout, and (3) integrates with prefill vs decode scheduling lanes (fastpass and steady lanes) to meet latency SLOs while maximizing token throughput and minimizing cost.
background: We observe bimodal seqlen distributions in several enterprise traffic patterns (short chat messages + long-context documents). Existing fixed bucketing causes either high padding waste (if wide buckets) or low GPU utilization (if many tiny buckets). Kernel selection currently uses static heuristics that don't consider microbatch composition or prefill/decoder mix; as a result, we sometimes pick a dense fused attention kernel on sparse-prefill-heavy minibatches, increasing runtime memory pressure and latency.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end scallop batching reduces average padding tokens per request by >= 28% on the sampled workloads
Scheduler uses kernel-hint for > 90% of scallop-shaped micro-batches and picks matching optimized kernels (fast sparse/dense)
Tail latency (p99) for interactive tier (fastpass) remains within current SLO (+5% allowed during experiments)
Integration tests for prefill/decode lane isolation and fallback when kernel not available
Dashboard shows token savings, kernel-choice distribution, and cost-per-token delta compared to baseline
implementation_notes: Scallop bucketer: build on histogram-driven splitter that inspects incoming request seqlen and produces 1..N scallops where each scallop holds contiguous prefix ranges to minimize per-scaffolding KV cache fragmentation

Micro-batch composer: accept scallops from multiple requests and co-schedule based on target kernel affinity + lane (fastpass vs steady). Use age-based hedging to avoid head-of-line blocking for interactive requests

Kernel hints: add small metadata tag (kernel_profile) per micro-batch describing target attention regime (dense-fused, sparse-strided, chunked-local) and expected max-seqlen; scheduler consults model/kernel catalog to pick best kernel and layout

Attention optimizations: integrate chunked local attention for scallops representing long-context tails and use prefix-shared KV caching for scallop prefixes to avoid re-serializing identical prefixes

Prefill/Decode scheduling: reserve N% of slots as fastpass lane for low-latency short scallops; steady lane aggregates longer scallops for better throughput. Implement fast fallback that demotes steady-lane scallops to smaller scallops when fast lane contention is high
Metrics: track padded_tokens_saved, kernel_hint_hit_rate, microbatch_utilization, p50/p95/p99 latency per lane, memory headroom per GPU, and cost_per_generated_token

Rollout plan: dark-launch scallop-hint metadata for 2 weeks, compare scheduling decisions vs baseline without changing runtime; next run limited canary to 5% of traffic, then ramp after quality checks
decision_log: Chosen scallop approach over aggressive truncation to preserve model quality on long-context requests (trade-off: slightly more scheduling complexity)
Kernel hints preferred to runtime auto-probing because probing adds significant latency variance under prefill workloads
Fastpass lane implemented as soft reservation (percent of concurrency) rather than hard slot reservation to keep throughput flexible under bursty load
tradeoffs: Complexity: scallop splitting and prefix KV sharing increases bookkeeping in runtime; mitigation: compact scallop descriptors and ephemerally pin KV entries only while active

Memory vs Latency: using specialized sparse kernels reduces compute but can increase memory overhead for index structures; we'll add high-water guardrails and fallback to dense kernels when memory headroom low
Scheduling fairness: prioritizing fastpass could starve background throughput; implement age-based hedging and periodic backfills

open_risks: KV cache fragmentation: scallop prefix sharing may increase invalidation churn under request cancellations
Kernel availability mismatch: some GPU instances lack optimized sparse kernels; need fallback heuristics to prevent tail explosion
Telemetry noise: attributing cost savings precisely to scallop changes vs steady lane tuning will require controlled A/B tests
review_feedback: Priya Natarajan (ML): request explicit eval on long-context QA tasks to ensure scallop splitting doesn't hurt retrieval grounding
Ethan Park (Infra): suggested adding per-GPU capability flags for kernel availability to scheduler rather than global assumptions
Lina Rodrigues (PM): asked for clearer rollout gating tied to cost-per-token improvement and error-rate thresholds
Security (A. Gupta): confirm scallop metadata does not leak PII and is sanitized before any logs exported
qa_plan: Unit tests for splitter/merger invariants (reconstructability of original sequence from scallops)
Integration tests: micro-batch composer with kernel_hint hot path and fallback path
Performance tests: p50/p95/p99 for fastpass and steady lanes under synthetic and sampled production traces
Quality tests: regression prompts for long-doc summarization, retrieval-augmented generation, and short-turn chat
